Neighbors compared; wrong order swapped; largest bubbles to end each pass.

sections.title: Mental model — three ways humans sort

blocks.md: Machine sorting copies three things you already do with hands: **picking smallest item repeatedly** (selection), **swapping neighbors until line ordered** (bubble), **sliding new card into sorted hand** (insertion). Every fancy sorter later is one of these ideas made smarter.
**Sorted part grows from one end; unsorted part shrinks. Every basic sort tells this same story.**

steps: Selection: scan rest → find min → swap to front slot → front moves right
Bubble: walk left-to-right swapping wrong neighbors → biggest lands at end → end moves left
Insertion: take next unsorted value → slide left past bigger ones → drop into gap

items.q: Which method never touches an element it already placed?
items.explain: Each selection pass fixes one FINAL position. Bubble/insertion placements can change later.

items.q: Which method slides elements RIGHT to open a gap?
items.explain: Insertion shifts bigger cards right while hunting the slot.

blocks.label: insertion sort

blocks.md: **Takeaway:** insertion LOVES almost-sorted data. Selection always does identical scanning. Bubble wastes swaps but has the easy early-exit.

items.q: How many swaps does selection sort do total on any input of size n?
items.explain: One swap per round — cheapest swap count, expensive comparisons.

items.q: Bubble inner loop bound `n-1-pass` exists because…
options: pass p already settled p largest at the tail
items.explain: No reason to re-compare frozen positions.

items.q: Insertion sort on {2,3,4,5,1}: how far does key=1 travel?
items.explain: Worst case for ONE card still cheap overall if rare.

items.q: Stable sort keeps equal items' original order. Which basics are naturally stable?
options: bubble & insertion (only swap when STRICTLY bigger)
items.explain: Swapping on ties would break stability; both skip ties.

sections.title: Counting work — same lens as Module 01

items: **Selection**: outer n rounds × inner scan up to n ⇒ pairs-style counting. Swaps tiny, comparisons heavy
**Bubble**: same pair-style worst day; early exit saves nearly-sorted days
**Insertion**: worst day pairs-style, but nearly-sorted day ≈ single pass

blocks.md: All three struggle when input big and scrambled — pairs-counting territory again. Smarter divide-and-conquer sorters arrive at L2; first master these three by hand.

items.q: 100,000 random numbers to sort — pick wisely:
options: any of the three basics fine
none acceptable — need smarter sorter (next level)
items.explain: Pairs-level work on 10⁵ = ~10¹⁰ steps. Freeze guaranteed.

items.title: Implement Selection Sort
items.statement: Code it, then print array after EVERY round.
hints: Track index of min, not value.

items.title: Bubble Sort + Swap Counter
items.statement: Sort ascending, output total swap count. Try {3,2,1} and {1,2,3} — explain difference.
hints: Sorted input = zero swaps + instant exit.

items.title: Insertion Sort Descending
items.statement: Same algorithm, biggest first. Flip exactly ONE comparison.

items.title: Sort Only Even Positions
items.statement: Elements at indices 0,2,4… sorted ascending; odd indices untouched.
hints: Copy evens out, sort, write back — or adapt loops stepping by 2.

items.title: K Passes of Bubble
items.statement: Run exactly k bubble passes; print result. Observe k biggest values settled right.
hints: Outer loop capped at k, not n−1.

items.title: Is Nearly Sorted?
items.statement: Count elements more than one position away from sorted spot; if ≤ k, declare 'nearly sorted'.
hints: This decides whether insertion is a smart real-world choice.

items.title: Stability Tester
items.statement: Sort pairs (score,id) by score using YOUR insertion sort; verify ids of equal scores stay original-ordered.
hints: Ties must NOT swap — strict comparison.

items.title: Min-Max in Fewest Comparisons (warm-up)
items.statement: Find both min and max; naive needs 2(n−1) checks — do better with pairwise trick (~3n/2).
hints: Process elements in PAIRS: compare pair first, then winners vs max, losers vs min.
Odd length: seed both with first element.

items.title: Move Zeros to End (stable)
items.statement: Push all zeros right preserving non-zero order — do NOT use library sort.

items.title: Chocolate Distribution
items.statement: Pick m packets minimizing max−min difference given to students. Sort first, then sliding window of size m.
hints: After sorting, answer = min over i of a[i+m−1]−a[i].
Sorting converts chaos into adjacent comparisons.

revisionCard: Selection: find-min + one swap per round; prefix becomes final
Bubble: neighbor swaps; tail settles; early-exit on clean pass
Insertion: slide-right + drop; loves nearly-sorted data
Stability = equal keys keep arrival order; strict comparisons protect it
All three = pairs-level worst case — big scrambled inputs need divide-and-conquer
sort() default ascending; custom lambda flips anything
